conviction_note: Mild positive lean from two counterparties that reported after Solar's H1 (AO Johansen raised its guide on strong Danish B2B demand and better gross margin; Rexel's Sweden and Benelux grew with significant price increases), offset by guidance arithmetic that makes a narrowing to the lower half plausible, and a stretched balance sheet that makes the cash line live. abs 5.5 is set on 'new numbers plus a likely guidance refinement' for a thin, highly levered equity, and is shaded down from the 7-9% base because this name's last two prints moved under 1%. p_up 56. The findings sum (+0.3) and the scaled number (+0.66) agree in sign; neither is fitted to the other.

findings.finding: Brødrene A&O Johansen, Solar's direct Danish competitor in electrical and VVS wholesale, reported on 28 Oct: Q3 2026 organic growth 12.5% (B2B organic 13.1%, B2B gross margin up to 22.2% from 21.3%), 'market activity remained high', and full-year guidance raised on Q3 'and the start of October'. Denmark is 33% of Solar's revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On observed release days Solar's Q3 prints moved -1.4% (2023-11-02), +3.7% (2024-10-31, EBITDA guide reconfirmed) and -1.9% (2025-11-06, guide narrowed). The last two prints (May and Aug 2026) moved under 1%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Solar rose 3.3% on 2026-10-29, the session after AO's release, on about twice its normal volume (31.9k shares against ~12k), then gave back 2.4% over the next two sessions. What is not priced is how much of AO's demand Solar Denmark captured: Solar's Danish organic growth was only +1.5% in Q2 while AO says it keeps gaining share, so this is a market read and not a Solar number. That caveat sets the size.
findings.independence: Rexel Q3 2026 (a different company and market, see the next finding): https://www.financialcontent.com/article/gnwcq-2026-10-22-rexel-q3-2026-sales

findings.finding: Rexel's Q3 2026 sales (22 Oct) show Sweden +4.8% same-day (9M +2.5%, so accelerating, 'driven by residential and infrastructure') and Benelux +7.5% (Netherlands HVAC, solar and EV), with 'significant selling price increases in both cable and non-cable products' across Europe. Sweden and the Netherlands are 17% and 23% of Solar's revenue, and price inflation underpins the inventory gains Solar flagged for Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same Q3 history as above. No observed reaction of Solar to Rexel releases (Solar was +0.5% on 2026-10-22).
findings.why_not_priced: This is a cross-border peer read that Danish small-cap holders rarely trade on: Solar closed 192.0 on 10-22 and 10-23, unchanged. It is a proxy, and the ~DKK 20m inventory gain in Q3 is already inside the company's guide, so the finding stays small.
findings.independence: AO Johansen Q3 (Danish market, different company): https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b4081f30b84806b5fd1fd509e422a2bc4&lang=en&src=listed

findings.finding: Solar filed no inside-information guidance adjustment between the H1 report (2026-08-13) and the eve of Q3, 34 days after quarter end. This company has used that channel before when it would miss: 'Adjustment of 2025 guidance due to unexpected market slowdown' on 2025-08-08, six days before H1, and 'Expectations for 2024 and preliminary results for 2023' on 2024-02-02. So the 400-480 range is very likely intact.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: When this channel was used, the stock fell 17.9% (2025-08-08) and about 25% over two sessions (2024-02-02/05). Absent a warning, guide-reconfirming prints moved +3.7% (Q3 2024) and -0.5% (Q2 2026).
findings.why_not_priced: The absence of a warning is public, so most of it is priced; the stock recovered from 188 in early October to 200.5. What remains is the left tail it removes, a FY miss. If the market believed a cut were coming, the stock would sit near its 2026 low and not 6% off it.

findings.finding: Guidance arithmetic leaves room for a narrowing below the sell-side number. H1 EBITDA was 143 (adjusted 212) 'at the lower end of our expected range'. The 440 midpoint needs H2 adjusted EBITDA of about 303 against 258 in H2 2025 (Q3 116 + Q4 142), i.e. +17%, while Q2 adjusted grew only +4% (122 vs 117). Solar narrowed into the lower half at Q3 2025 (to ~460 inside 450-510; stock -1.9%), and the only sell-side number found (4 analysts, 462, snippet only) sits above the midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 narrowing into the lower half: -1.9% (2025-11-06), then -2.6% on the placing a week later. FY guide below expectations: -10.9% (2026-02-05) and -7.6% (2025-02-06).
findings.why_not_priced: The bar is unsourced beyond one dated aggregator snippet, so this finding is capped. The 20-day run-up (+6.2%) and the AO-day jump suggest holders are leaning toward a reconfirmation, not a lower-half narrowing. If a cut to the low end were priced, the stock would not have retraced to the post-February-guide level of about 200 from 188.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 precedent of a Q3 narrowing: https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b82604d564f94ccae0697014ae5908749&lang=en&src=listed

findings.finding: The cash line is live: H1 2026 operating cash flow was -440m with a ~250m inventory pre-buy, gearing was 5.1x against a 1-3x target, and undrawn facilities fell to DKK 512m from 718m. The company says the inventory build 'is expected to normalise during H2', so the Q3 cash flow and working capital are a line the release must carry.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior: Q3 2025 OCF +64m with the stock -1.9% on the narrowing; Q3 2024 OCF -196m with the stock +3.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: Financing treated as a question: the money funds an inventory pre-buy ahead of supplier price increases (the source of the flagged inventory gains) and receivables from returning growth, both corroborated by AO and Rexel. The company guided the reversal, so the expected sign is near zero. The small negative reflects the leverage tail (a Luceco-style cash disappointment) on a 5.1x-geared equity that raised equity a week after last year's Q3.

outside_window.finding: Risk of another directed share issue: last year Solar launched a 646,000-share directed issue on 2025-11-11, five sessions after its Q3 report (stock -2.6% that day), and gearing is now higher (5.1x against 3.4x then). Any repeat would almost certainly land after the 2026-11-03 close.
